title: Suboccipital muscles (posterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Lateral part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
Extends the head and turns the face to the same side.
hy: The vertebral artery and the suboccipital nerve (C1) lie on the posterior arch of the atlas in the floor of the suboccipital triangle, which this muscle bounds with the two obliques.

rows: Medial part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
Extends the head. It is small and works mainly to steady the head on the atlas.
Occipital bone, between the superior and inferior nuchal lines.
Extends the head and bends it to its own side.
Turns the atlas, and with it the head and face, to the same side. Despite its name it does not reach the skull.
Lower half of the ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes of C7 to T3.
Mastoid process of the temporal bone and the lateral third of the superior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves.
Both sides together extend the head and neck. One side alone bends the head to that side and turns the face to the same side.
Transverse processes of T1 to T5 and articular processes of C4 to C7.
Back edge of the mastoid process of the temporal bone, under cover of splenius capitis and sternocleidomastoid.
Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves.
Both sides together extend the head. One side alone bends the head to its own side and turns the face to the same side.
